candidates.name: Squamous Cell Carcinoma
support_spans: Classic-appearing hyperkeratotic lesion with many pseudohorn cysts
Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells originated from one lateral end, pushing down into the dermis and involving many hairs
Malignant squamous cells contained eosinophilic cytoplasm and prominent nucleoli; mitotic figures were present
candidates.why: The histopathological examination reveals a hyperkeratotic lesion with pseudohorn cysts and proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells, which are characteristic features of Squamous Cell Carcinoma.

candidates.name: Sebaceous carcinoma
support_spans: Central areas of clear cell change were periodic acid–Schiff positive and diastase sensitive
contradict_spans: Negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor
candidates.why: The presence of clear cell change with positive periodic acid-Schiff and diastase sensitive staining suggests sebaceous carcinoma, but the negative immunohistochemical stains for adipophilin and androgen receptor contradict this diagnosis.

candidates.name: Basal cell carcinoma
support_spans: Ki67 highlighted scattered basal cells and stained about 20% to 40% of tumor cell nuclei
contradict_spans: Proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells originated from one lateral end, pushing down into the dermis and involving many hairs
candidates.why: The Ki67 staining pattern suggests basal cell carcinoma, but the proliferation of neoplastic squamous cells contradicts this diagnosis.
